# One filler per key, however many askers arrive

## WHY

An entry expires at `t`. At `t + ε` every request for that key misses at once — and with a cache in
front of the store precisely because the key is hot, that is not one fill, it is the whole request
rate. The store sees the spike the cache was supposed to prevent; on a slow store it may not
survive it. The name for this is the thundering herd, and the fix is older than the name: the first
asker fills, everybody else waits for that fill.

What the cache needs is one bit of state per key — *somebody is already filling this* — and a rule
that is easy to get wrong in two directions:

- **the marker must be per key.** A global "filling" flag serialises unrelated keys, which turns the
  cache into a single-threaded bottleneck;
- **the waiter must not become a second filler.** Registering every asker as a filler passes a
  "no duplicate fill" test that only checks the first two calls, and then fills five times under
  load.

This step is the bookkeeping, not the async: the marker is a set of keys, the decision is an enum,
and the spec drives it by hand. The runtime that makes a waiter actually wait arrives with the
service; the state machine is the same, and it is the part that is hard to see when the code is
buried in `async` plumbing.

## TASK

The scaffold added `src/single_flight.rs` and its `pub mod single_flight;` line. `InFlight::begin` is
the stub; `InFlight::complete` and the accessors are given.

- **[`InFlight::begin`]** — mark the key and answer [`Decision::Fill`] when nobody is filling it;
  answer [`Decision::Wait`] when somebody is, and do not mark it a second time.
- **A completed fill frees the key** — `complete` removes the marker and answers whether it was
  there; the next `begin` fills again.
- **Two keys are independent** — filling `a` says nothing about `b`.

## DONE WHEN

- `kiln run cache/6.3-single-flight` — the spec passes
- `kiln check cache/6.3-single-flight` — every must gate is green, including the gates this step
  introduces for the rest of the track

## TRAP

1. **A waiter registered as a filler.** `if !self.filling.contains(key) { self.filling.insert(...) }`
   is correct only if the insert happens once; a version that inserts unconditionally and then asks
   `len == 1` passes the two-call test and fails the ten-waiter one.
2. **A global flag.** `if self.filling.is_empty()` serialises every key: the spec's
   *"two keys fill independently"* fails, and so does the cache under two hot keys.
3. **Forgetting to complete.** The marker is only removed by `complete`; a fill path that returns an
   error without calling it leaves the key permanently "in flight" — every asker waits forever, and
   the spec's *"after completion every waiter is a filler again"* is the visible half of that bug.
4. **Clearing the whole set on complete.** `self.filling.clear()` passes the single-key tests and
   breaks every other in-flight fill.

## FURTHER

- [Single-flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-flight_pattern) — the pattern, and the async
  versions that share one future between waiters
- [`BTreeSet`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.BTreeSet.html) — `insert` returns
  whether the value was new, which is the entire decision here
- [Go: `singleflight`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight) — the same state machine
  with a result type, and the error-sharing question this probe leaves out
